key_insight: AutoEnergyDesign uses an LLM agent to optimize building energy systems, reaching a roughly €3.53 million net present cost—1.20% below the best TPE result.
engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce expensive simulation calls when sizing integrated energy technologies, including photovoltaics, batteries and heat pumps.
method: Propose configuration changes using prior simulation outcomes and structured memory.
Evaluate eight energy technologies through annual simulations and a 25-year cost objective.
Keep successful changes, revert unsuccessful ones with git, and record auditable decision traces.
evidence_signal: On one measured-load case study, three LLM variants ran 10 trials of 50 simulations each; median time to within 1% of the best design ranged from 18 to 27.5 simulations, versus 192 among successful evolution-strategy seeds.
watch_item: Results concern integrated building energy systems, not solar-cell devices, and broader validation is needed beyond the single case study.
paper_title: AutoEnergyDesign: An LLM-Driven Agent for Automatic Energy System Design Optimization
